title: Arcturus Expands Meiji Collaboration With $50 Million Investment
summary: Arcturus Therapeutics expands its Meiji Seika Pharma collaboration, including a $50 million equity investment at an 80% premium.
body_markdown:
Alongside the investment, the two companies entered into an exclusive license agreement relating to the application of Arcturus' ARCT-154 technology for an undisclosed therapeutic area, under which, the filing states, Meiji will be responsible for development and commercialization at its cost. They also signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) setting out the principal terms for a potential collaboration and license agreement for a pandemic preparedness and response program in Japan using the Arcturus platform. The filing states that neither party is obligated to enter into that definitive agreement.


Meiji agreed not to sell or transfer the shares through the 365th day following the date of the purchase agreement, and to standstill provisions for 24 months following the closing, according to the filing.


## Why It Matters for ARCT


"Alongside our CF program, these proceeds will be used to accelerate development of ARCT-2601 for OTC deficiency, the first mRNA therapeutic to utilize our LUNAR 2.0 delivery platform," said Joseph Payne, President and Chief Executive Officer of Arcturus. The company said the proceeds are also meant to clinically validate its LUNAR 2.0 next-generation mRNA platform. Payne said the investment, the license agreement and the MOU "reflects Meiji's confidence in our development capabilities and the potential of our technology platform."
